CH 02 · Featured project

STATIC

A mystery detective horror set in a remote Alaskan town, where an unseen force reaches through the television signal, abducting people without a trace. As reality begins to unravel, you must investigate the disappearances, uncover the truth behind the enigmatic Gray Signal, and decide the fate of a town haunted by its past.

01

Genre, Gameplay Mechanics, and Story

STATIC is a third-person mystery-horror adventure that blends investigation, survival, and action into a narrative-driven experience where every major decision carries lasting consequences.

Genre
Mystery-horror adventure
Perspective
Third-person
Players
Single-player
For fans of
Alan Wake · Heavy Rain · The Vanishing of Ethan Carter

Story

STATIC is built on the events of the novel Myst, but instead of retelling its story, it invites players to rewrite it. The game follows the same world, characters, and central mystery while allowing pivotal choices to reshape the narrative and the destiny of the heroes.


In 2018, Saoirse Barrell returns to the Alaskan town Mag Point: the place she swore never to see again. Ten years earlier, her ten-year-old brother, Caleb, vanished without a trace alongside four other children. The town never found answers, and neither did she. Ironically, she comes back for something utterly mundane: to retrieve her old medical records. The moment she arrives, people begin disappearing again. When Saoirse's father becomes the prime suspect, she is forced to launch her own investigation.


She finds an ally in Ian Demme, her former high school boyfriend. Ten years ago, she left Mag Point without saying goodbye, shattering his life and leaving wounds that never truly healed. Their unexpected reunion forces them to confront both their shared past and the secrets they have kept from one another.


As the mysterious Gray Signal spreads through the town again, Ian and Saoirse must uncover the truth behind the disappearances that have haunted the town for decades. But in STATIC, the truth is never fixed. Every crucial decision has the power to alter relationships, reshape the investigation, and change the fate of their loved ones.

Two protagonists, one town

Players explore the isolated Alaskan town of Mag Point, uncovering clues behind a series of mysterious disappearances while confronting hostile entities emerging from the enigmatic Gray Signal. The story is experienced through two playable protagonists, Ian and Saoirse, whose gameplay styles complement one another.

Ian Demme

Action · Close quarters · Investigation

A young local troublemaker. He anchors the game's tense investigation line and its close-quarters encounters, relying on firearms and hand-to-hand combat when the threat gets physical.

Saoirse Barrell

Stealth · Observation · Narrative

Reluctantly returned after years in New York City, she approaches danger through stealth, observation, and careful infiltration, offering a contrasting perspective on both the narrative and the gameplay.

Gameplay

The core gameplay is built around five interconnected pillars.

Investigation20%

Collecting evidence and reconstructing events on a detective board to identify suspects, motives, and hidden connections.

Narrative25%

Branching dialogue, cinematic sequences, and character relationships that shape both the immediate story and the ending.

Exploration25%

Searching locations, environmental storytelling, hidden documents, and optional discoveries.

Combat15%

Firearm and hand-to-hand encounters centered primarily around Ian's gameplay.

Stealth15%

Infiltration, evasion, and silent navigation, primarily experienced through Saoirse.

A living world

The world itself is dynamic. Locations can be explored during both day and night, and the transition between them fundamentally changes the experience. Areas that are safe during daylight may become hostile after dark, introducing new enemies and altered routes, that question the very nature of reality. You can never be certain how much of what you're experiencing is real. Players will encounter environmental changes, and previously inaccessible opportunities. Players are encouraged to revisit familiar locations under different conditions, as the town itself evolves alongside the story.

Innovative mechanics

Two systems set STATIC apart from a traditional detective horror.

The Gray Signal

A mysterious phenomenon that obscures hostile entities from normal perception. During both combat and stealth encounters, players must actively operate a retransmission device to intercept the Gray Signal, revealing enemies that would otherwise remain invisible. Maintaining the signal becomes a constant tactical consideration, transforming every encounter into a balance between awareness, survival, and resource management.

The investigation board

Unlike conventional detective games, the investigation board provides no guidance, hints, or hidden validation. Players independently connect evidence and formulate conclusions, making genuine deductions instead of following predetermined solutions. Three pivotal investigation decisions serve as major narrative turning points. An incorrect conclusion does not result in failure or a game over. Instead, the story branches in a different direction.

Your Conclusion Has Altered The Story

Interactive dialogue

Two main playable characters, Ian and Saoirse cross paths by chance in Mag Point for the first time since 2008, when Saoirse left for New York City without a word, abandoning both the town and the relationship they once shared. 04

Character files

Dossiers on the game characters: who they are, how they speak, and what they say under pressure. Voice guides and systemic barks for each.

Ian Demme

Protagonist - action, investigation · 28

Bio

28, lifelong resident of Mag Point and a graduate of White High School. After the traumatic events of August 2008, he spent nearly a year at the Alaska Psychiatric Institute in Anchorage before returning to his hometown.

He is one of the few people who knows the truth about the Gray Signal and its connection to the town's disappearances. Although he has uncovered fragments of the mystery, his primary concern is protecting his younger brother, Victor, whom he believes is now in danger.

Voice

  • • Speaks in short, deliberate sentences. Says only what matters.
  • • Distrustful by instinct. Rarely explains himself unless absolutely necessary.
  • • Grounded, practical vocabulary.
  • • Constantly alert. Notices details others dismiss.
  • • Around Saoirse, he is confused and lost.
Says

"Everything I'm about to tell you would sound insane. You'd question every word."

Never says

"I don't know what else to do. I ran out of ideas."

Barks

combat · spotted"There. Keep your head down."
combat · reload"Come on... Come on, damn it!"
combat · enemy down"*spits*"
combat · enemy boss"And I thought you'd be taller."
stealth · near-miss"Shit... That was too close..."
explore · clue found"I'll take it. Could be useful."
explore · landmark"We used to go there back in school. Remember that?"
signal rising"Hear that? We better keep moving."
idle"Why am I still here?"

Relationships

Saoirse: his former high school girlfriend who broke his heart. He is still in love with her and holds on to the memories of their past. Talks to her in apologetic tone. Never looks her in the eye.


Capt. Maisey: the only cop he doesn't needle, and the only one who will lend a helping hand.


Donal Hockley: his former classmate and a close friend. Together they started the investigation into the disappearances, but something happened between them. They rarely talk.

Saoirse Barrell

Protagonist - stealth, narrative · 27

Bio

27, a New York City resident and a graduate of Columbia University. She shares an apartment with her boyfriend, Rust. Born and raised in Mag Point, she has spent the last decade trying to erase the town from her life. To Saoirse, Mag Point is a place of grief and memories best left buried. She returns only because her cardiologist has requested her original paper medical records, forcing her back to the hometown.

Expected to stay in Mag Point for no more than three days. Instead, a series of unsettling coincidences traps her in town. Her father, Val Barrell, is arrested by the local police as the prime suspect in the abduction of a young boy. Saoirse has no choice but to remain and uncover the truth before it's too late.

Voice

  • • Speaks with a distinct New York accent. Confident and articulate, often coming across as arrogant or dismissive.
  • • Her voice turns sharp and steely whenever she needs something or takes control of a situation.
  • • Usually composed and emotionally restrained, but when pushed too far, she doesn't hesitate to swear.
  • • Exceptionally gentle and affectionate with the people she loves.
  • • She never has a single kind word to say about Mag Point.
Says

"Now listen, you have absolutely no right to keep my dad under custody unless you press charges!"

Never says

"Deep down... I've missed this place."

Barks

stealth · hiding"Quiet... Be very still..."
stealth · near-miss"...Okay. That was close."
stealth · distraction"Focus, Saoirse!"
combat · forced fight"Think girls can't fight back?"
explore · clue found"See what the MPPD thinks about that."
explore · old spot"Enough memories for the day..."
signal rising"It's gotten louder! Did you notice?"
idle"I wish I'd never come here in the first place."

Relationships

Ian: Saoirse's high school boyfriend during their senior year at White High School. When she left Mag Point, she never told him she was leaving. Seeing him again after ten years is the last thing she wanted. To Saoirse, Ian is a living reminder of the past she worked so hard to escape.


Donal Hockley: A former classmate and one of Saoirse's closest friends in high school. During their senior year, tensions between Donal, Ian, and Saoirse drove a wedge between them. Despite the years apart, Saoirse still speaks to Donal with warmth and genuine affection.

Donal Hockley

Friendly NPC · 28

Bio

28, graduated alongside Ian Demme and Saoirse Barrell at White High School. Once Ian's closest friend, Donal chose a different path after graduation, serving as a psychologist in the United States Coast Guard. After leaving the service, he returned to Mag Point and decided to stay.

As a senior, Donal investigated the unexplained disappearances that had haunted Mag Point for decades. His independent research uncovered a disturbing pattern behind the incidents, one that points directly toward the mystery of the Gray Signal.

Voice

  • • Thick, deep voice. Speaks with pauses, thinking beforehand.
  • • Shy and unsure around former classmates.

Barks

greeting"Hey... It's been a minute, right?"
questioned"You remember, huh? I'm genuinely surprised."
deflecting"Why the sudden change of heart?"
conflict"Little shits... Get out of here now!"

Capt. Keith Maisey

Friendly NPC, Mag Point PD · 43

Bio

43, commands the Mag Point Police Department. A lifelong resident of Mag Point, he is a devoted husband and the father of two daughters.

In 2008, Maisey led the response to the August disappearances. During the investigation, his officers were ambushed by Faraday Kavanagh, a grieving father whose son had vanished. A decade later, the memory of that day still haunts him.

Voice

  • • Sharp around the edges. Capable of raising his voice in a critical situation.
  • • Looks you directly in the eye when he speaks.

Barks

handing over a file"You didn't get this from me. In fact, you never got it from anyone."
radio · checking in"Maisey here. No. Still nothing."
warning the pair"Whatever you two are doing, I don't want to know. Just do it quietly."
command"Set up a perimeter. Report 10-79."

05

Collectibles

A showcase of findable items and their examine texts. In STATIC, objects carry the story sideways. Each description is written to do two jobs at once: tell the player what they're holding, and let slip a fragment of history nobody says out loud. Click an item to examine it; click the image to enhance it.

Hockey puck with "Alaska Aces" logo

Evidence — Sidewalk outside Colin Hall's house

Kyren Hall's hockey puck.

His dad, Colin Hall, caught this puck at the Alaska Aces game against the Orson Hunters. That was the night Kyren decided he would become a professional hockey player someday.

Kyren has been missing for two days.


Ian: "Val only helped the boy fish it out of the drain. No good deed goes unpunished."

Ian Demme ICE Card

Document — Ian's wallet, behind Saoirse's photograph

My name is Ian Demme. I have a serious mental disorder. If you find me sitting or lying motionless, unresponsive, and unable to blink, I am experiencing a temporary catatonic episode. It usually lasts between twenty minutes and one hour. I am not dangerous. Please stay with me until I regain consciousness, or call an ambulance.

This emergency card was issued to Ian upon his discharge from the Alaska Psychiatric Institute. More than once, it has saved his life.


Reggie: "I'd have left you lying there if I hadn't read that you're not all there. Got it?"

front

Photograph of Saoirse

Keepsake — Ian's wallet

A worn photograph of Saoirse Barrell that Ian keeps tucked inside his wallet.

He took it himself when they were both seventeen and in love. He has carried it ever since. In a life stripped of almost everything worth holding onto, the memories are all he has left.


Reggie: "Pretty girl. Yours? ...Yeah, don't strain yourself, I get it. I'm not an idiot."

On the back is Reggie's phone number written by himself. He said he has a motorboat for sale. It might come in handy.

Plush toy heart

Keepsake — Ian's room

A small plush heart Saoirse gave Ian on Valentine's Day.

Before handing it to him, she sprayed it with the perfume Ian had given her. The fragrance has long since faded, and the little toy is worn and frayed with age. It still sits on a shelf in Ian's living room. It's the only shelf in the house untouched by dust.


Saoirse: "It was such a silly little gift. But Ian absolutely loved it."

Prescription bottle

Personal effect — Ian's bathroom cabinet

Ian's name is printed on the prescription label, yet the bottle is still full.

Prescribed in 2008. The seal was not broken until 2018. They are supposed to make the hallucinations easier to endure.


Ian: "Damn smug shrinks... Those pills only make things worse..."

Saoirse's medical records

Document — Mag Point hospital

A folder with Saoirse's old medical records.

During an appointment at a cardiology center in NYC, the doctor asked Saoirse to retrieve her original paper records to confirm the best course of treatment for her heart condition. That request forced Saoirse to return to the hometown she'd sworn never to see again.


Saoirse: "Mom, do you realize I have to go back to that shithole just to grab a notebook with a diagnosis everyone already knows?"

Ian's swimming goggles

Keepsake — Ian's parents' house

An old pair of swimming goggles.

Back in 2007, Ian wore them when he defeated Norman Petrich, the Southeast Alaska regional champion who came within a hair of making the U.S. Olympic swimming team. They are a reminder of the greatest victory of his youth, and of everything he lost afterward.


Ian: "Why the hell do they still keep this junk? It belongs in the trash. Just like me."

Key from Creed's study

Key — Creed Clemens's house, in a bathrobe pocket

A brass key stained with a green patina.

It unlocks the door to Creed Clemens's study on the second floor of his house. Creed can no longer remember what is so important inside. Alzheimer's has stolen that from him. Yet of one thing he is certain: if he doesn't get into that room soon, something terrible will happen.


Paige: "And just what is so important in your old study that makes you climb to the second floor? Shame on you, Mr. Clemens!"

Crystal Peak VHS tape

Tape — August Pruett's house

A VHS tape that somehow survived the fire at Crystal Peak Station.

It was recorded as part of an official report documenting the attempt to decipher the intercepted signal. Only the first twenty minutes contain footage. The rest of the tape is blank.


Ian: "Twenty minutes. Somebody watched the rest and made sure nobody else would."

06

Screenplay scene

Screenplay scene: the same scene that runs as an interactive dialogue, written as linear film script. This is the canonical cut: the version where Ian decides to tell Saoirse the truth about the disappearances and pays for it. Margin notes mark where the canonical script and the game scenarios part ways.

STATIC — 'The Drive' (canonical cut)Excerpt · 3 pages

INT. IAN'S PICKUP — PARKED ON THE SOKOLOV HIGHWAY — NIGHT

Rain. Twenty yards back, a car sits crumpled against the guardrail, a police cruiser idling beside it, light bar sweeping the trees.

Ian climbs in, locks his hands on the steering wheel. Doesn't start the engine. Beside him: SAOIRSE BARRELL, bag on her lap, eyes on the floor mat. Neither speaks. The silence gets heavy enough to hear.

Saoirse clears her throat.

SAOIRSE

(quietly, not looking up)

Thanks for stopping to help us.

IAN

(wooden)

Yeah.

SAOIRSE

I'll probably just ask the officer to give me a ride to the hotel.

Ian turns away, forehead against his palm.

IAN

They're about to head into the woods. Looking for whoever it was you saw on the road.

(a whisper, mostly to himself)

Not that there's any point.

In the playable version this beat is the player's first choice: three ways to answer her.Play the scene →

SAOIRSE

I'll wait.

Her hand finds the door handle. It's already a goodbye.

IAN

That's hours. I'll drive you.

He starts the engine before she can answer - decision made the only way he can make one, fast and forward. The pickup swings slowly toward town.

IAN (CONT'D)

The Central?

Saoirse nods.

INT. IAN'S PICKUP — MOVING — NIGHT

Wipers. Road noise. Two people not talking, loudly.

Saoirse studies Ian from the passenger seat when he isn't looking. Whatever she's remembering - the handsome cheerful guy with a charming smile - it isn't what's driving this truck: gaunt, unshaven, hair nobody's touched in weeks, mean stare.

Without thinking, Ian fishes a cigarette from his pocket. Lights it one-handed. Saoirse immediately coughs.

IAN

(voice cracked)

Sorry.

He cracks the window, flicks the cigarette out.

SAOIRSE

(narrowing her eyes)

You never smoked before...

Ian rolls his neck. Gives his passenger a first, brief glance.

IAN

Yeah, well...

The pause comes back. This time it's Ian who can't stand it.

IAN (CONT'D)

Not how you remembered me, huh? Go ahead, tell me I look like shit. At least we'd be clear on one thing.

Saoirse says nothing.

Ian spins the wheel; the pickup jolts over a speed bump and pulls into the lot of a four-story hotel. He brakes, kills the ignition, and turns to her, meeting her eyes for the first time.

He's made a decision.

IAN (CONT'D)

(hoarse)

Saoirse. I don't know why you came back, and I'm not going to ask. But there's something you need to know. Whatever killed Caleb and the others ten years ago - it's back in Mag Point.

INT. IAN'S PICKUP — HOTEL PARKING LOT — CONTINUOUS

Stillness. Rain on the roof.

SAOIRSE

What did you just say?

Ian pulls a slow breath through his nose. Starts again.

IAN

Whatever killed Caleb and the others—

SAOIRSE

(quiet; iron)

Shut up. Shut up. Shut your filthy mouth.

Ian rocks back like he's taken one on the jaw. She's glaring at him from under her brow, and something in her eyes has caught fire.

IAN

(rasping)

Saoirse—

SAOIRSE

(shrieking; the control snaps)

I said shut up! Don't you dare put my name in that dirty mouth of yours! Or my brother's! You— you— you're nothing, how dare you! You made this up on the drive over, didn't you?! So I'd believe you and fall into bed with you - like you wanted back then, after prom!

IAN

(barely audible; white as chalk)

But I—

SAOIRSE

Shut it, Demme! Look at yourself, you freak! You make me sick, you always made me sick! Always, you hear me?! I only went out with you out of pity, because nobody else would ever look at you! Nobody!

In the game this eruption scales with a hidden counter: the crueler the ride, the crueler the speech. On the page there is only one version: the worst one.

She gropes behind her for the door handle, yanks at it, frantic.

SAOIRSE (CONT'D)

I knew I'd have the bad luck of seeing your face when I flew out here. I knew it! Rot in this shithole, son of a bitch! I hate you!

The door gives. Slams. Through the streaked glass: her silhouette shrinking into the rain, bag on her shoulder, until the fog takes it.

Ian doesn't move. The wipers count. He sits there long after there's nothing left to look at.
